_comment: Single source of truth for the render. Every visual is derived from `seed`, so an unchanged config must produce a byte-identical screenshot. If it does not, something is reading an unseeded RNG.

terrain._comment: region_size * vertex_spacing = world units per region. 4 x 4 regions of 1024 verts at 1.0 spacing => a 4096-unit map spanning -2048..2048, same extent as before but at 2x mesh density (1.0 matches Terrain3D's own default; 2.0 under-sampled the ridged mountain noise into visibly faceted slopes).

continent._comment: Radial falloff from the map centre makes the landmass an island. The warp noise pushes that radius in and out so the coastline is ragged instead of circular.

plains._comment: Low-amplitude rolling ground covering most of the landmass.

mountains._comment: Ridged noise gated by a low-frequency belt mask. belt_low/high select roughly the top quarter of the belt noise - open them up and mountains swallow the entire map, which is the single easiest way to lose the campaign-map read.

material._comment: Terrain3D shader uniforms, reachable only via set_shader_param (they do not appear in `make api`). Deliberately excluded from the region cache hash - none of these change the heightmap or control map, they only affect how it is shaded.

palette._comment: Texture ids match the order of the assets built in terrain_builder. The reference map is arid: tan owns the plains and green is confined to wetter low ground, which is what stops it reading as generic green terrain.

forests._comment: Density mask decides where woods cluster; the height/slope gate then rejects surf and bare peaks. max_height is the treeline and should sit just under where snow starts blending (palette.snow_height - snow_blend), so forests stop before the mountains go white.
forests._species_comment: Species split. conifer_height_fraction is where conifers take over as a fraction of the min..max_height band, blended over conifer_blend_fraction either side. Altitude alone is not enough - the slope gate rejects most high ground, so a pure height split leaves the conifer pool nearly empty - hence a separate low-frequency stand field that seeds conifer woods in the lowlands too. Raise conifer_stand_threshold for fewer, smaller stands.
forests._lod_comment: Trees are grouped into lod_cell_size x lod_cell_size grid cells per species (one MultiMesh draw call per cell instead of per species), so visibility_range_end can drop whole cells once they're farther than view_distance from the camera rather than paying to draw all ~4500 trees regardless of where the camera is looking. view_distance_margin cross-fades the cut so cells don't hard-pop; set view_distance to 0 to disable culling entirely.

canopy._comment: Trees are built from `<kind>_cards` single-leaf quads scattered over a canopy shell, each sampling one leaf cell that tools/fetch_foliage.py segmented out of the Poly Haven atlas. radius_fraction is the shell radius and leaf_fraction the size of one leaf, both as a fraction of tree_height; base_fraction is how far down the trunk the foliage starts, as a fraction of trunk height (below 1.0 buries the bare pole). Card counts are per-kind because a conifer spire needs many small twigs to read as solid while a broadleaf dome needs fewer, larger fronds. Raising cards is the direct dial for how dense a wood reads from above; it costs 2 triangles per card per tree.

cities._comment: Cities are placed by dart throwing with a minimum separation, gated on flat-ish ground clear of the surf and below the hills. max_slope_degrees is deliberately tight - a settlement draped over a hillside reads as scattered rubble from above. Houses/keeps are assembled from the Quaternius kit (world/cities.gd, assets/buildings/kit/ - run `make buildings`); building_color/keep_color are gone since the kit's own materials replace them. building_size is still the tuning knob for how big a building reads - it is matched internally to the old procedural roof's diameter (size*1.9) so this didn't need to change when the geometry did.

network._comment: Rivers run downhill from high ground; roads are a minimum spanning tree over the cities; borders are the boundary of a nearest-city Voronoi partition. y_offset lifts each ribbon clear of the terrain - drop it to zero and they z-fight into stipple.

borders._comment: Grid cell edges are chained into polylines and smoothed before drawing; without smoothing_passes the boundary is a hard axis-aligned staircase. cell_size was 46 with 6 passes and still stair-stepped visibly in ridge.png - a coarser grid plus more passes reads as a soft tapered ribbon instead.

debug._comment: Terrain3D debug overlays, for splitting 'the lighting is wrong' from 'the control map is wrong'. One of: none, grey, control, heightmap, colormap, checkered, autoshader. Must be `none` for a golden shot.

water._comment: Colours are graded by reconstructed water depth, so shallow_color is what you see over the beach shelf and deep_color is open sea. extent_multiplier pushes the plane past the terrain so the horizon is water, not the region edge.

lighting._comment: Low sun angle gives the long directional shadows that make ridgelines readable from a high camera.

sky._comment: PhysicalSkyMaterial. Turbidity is the haze dial - low is a clean alpine sky, high is humid and washed out. ground_color is what the lower hemisphere contributes to ambient, so it wants to resemble the terrain rather than being neutral grey.

sdfgi._comment: min_cell_size is in world units and drives everything: cascade0 covers roughly min_cell_size * 64, each further cascade doubles it. At 8.0 with 6 cascades the last cascade spans ~16k units, comfortably past the 4096-unit map. Terrain detail below one cell is invisible to GI, which is fine - this is for large-scale bounce, not contact detail (that is SSAO/SSIL's job).

ssao._comment: radius is world units. The 1.0 Godot default is sized for a person-scale interior and does nothing here; this needs to span the folds between terrain vertices and the base of a city wall.

ssil._comment: Coloured short-range bounce. Off by default: its effect is sub-pixel from the overview camera while it costs a full screen pass, and it was a measurable part of a 20-minute three-preset render. Turn it on for close work.

volumetric_fog._comment: length must reach past the far ridges from the overview camera or the fog stops in mid-air partway across the map. density is ~150x below Godot's default because optical depth is density*distance and the volume being filled is kilometres deep, not room-sized: 0.002 over a 6000-unit length is optical depth 12, i.e. fully opaque grey. Measured usable range here is 0.00004 (imperceptible) to 0.00012 (washed out).
